title: First saxophone job at the Entertainers Cafe
summary: He played his first sax job at the Entertainers Cafe on Basin Street, which ran from the mid-1920s into the 1930s.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Well, too, John Henry, we're talking about Earl Piffson, you say something about him?

Yeah, he's the first one that showed me how to finger saxophone. From then on, I had, like I said, I had it on three weeks and I would play my first job. And there was no set up either because I would play it at the Entertainer's Cavalry. All the musicians come. All Creed and all Colour went there. Jammed back all night. What was that? It was on Basin Street, Basin between Iverville and Bainville. There was a place, John Henry, I'll talk about that, the Entertainer's Cavalry.
How long was that place? That was early at John Henry, all the time. Then he could have been talking about B-25 because that's in the next block from there.
How long was this Entertainer's Cavalry going? Do you remember?

Before the Entertainer's, the Entertainer's, I must have started around 25, 1925, 24. And then it lasted until up in the 30s. Yeah, it was up in the 30s because I left here in 31. Went to St. Louis and it was running when I left. So I stayed in 10 to 12 years.
